title: Held renewals and bridge supplies: class figures for Prescriptions & Renewals
content:
Patient Services Center desk guidance. When a Prescriptions & Renewals renewal is on hold, each prescription class fixes how quickly the patient is told why, how many calendar days the hold may run before it lapses, and whether a bridge supply exists for the class, how many days it dispenses and how many one prescription may receive in a rolling 12 months.

| Class | Patient told why the renewal is on hold within (business days) | Hold may run (calendar days) | Bridge supply allowed | Bridge fill (days' supply) | Bridge supplies per prescription in a rolling 12 months |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Acute Short-Course Prescription | 1 | 0 | no | 0 | 0 |
| Standard Maintenance Prescription | 1 | 30 | yes | 30 | 1 |
| Monitored Maintenance Prescription | 1 | 21 | yes | 30 | 1 |
| Schedule III-V Controlled Prescription | 1 | 14 | no | 0 | 0 |
| Schedule II Controlled Prescription | 1 | 14 | no | 0 | 0 |
| Specialty Medication Prescription | 1 | 21 | no | 0 | 0 |

**How the desk reads these figures.**

- The notification figure is the same for every class: 1 business day.
- The hold figure is the number of calendar days a renewal may stay on hold awaiting its missing requirement before it lapses.
- A bridge supply is a one-time fill that may be authorized while a renewal is on hold awaiting a visit or a lab. Only the Standard Maintenance Prescription and the Monitored Maintenance Prescription allow one; for both, the bridge fill is 30 days' supply and the cap is 1 per prescription in a rolling 12 months.
- For the classes marked "no", both bridge figures show 0.
